terminals.lead: Every terminal you manage, with live status. Open one for its settings, or select several to configure or update them together.
terminals.search: Search by name, IP or serial number
terminals.noneFound: No terminals found on the local networks.
terminals.empty: No terminals yet. Scan the network or add one by its IP address.
terminals.confirmRemove: Remove the selected terminals ({{n}}) from the list? The terminals themselves are not changed.
terminals.bulkConfigureHint: Sends the same server settings to every selected terminal, one after the other, using each terminal's saved barrier.
terminals.keepBarrierHint: Leave empty to keep each terminal's current barrier.
terminals.bulkUpdateHint: Signs the image once and installs it on every selected terminal, one after the other. Each terminal restarts after its update.
terminals.autoRefresh: Status is refreshed automatically every few seconds.

barrierState.saved: The barrier is saved on this computer. Diagnostics, configuration and updates work without typing it.
barrierState.missing: No barrier saved. Save it to see diagnostics and to change settings or firmware.
barrierState.rejected: The terminal rejected the saved barrier. Enter the current one.

terminal.barrierHint: Checked against the terminal, then stored only on this computer (app/data). It is never shown again.

barrierErrors.locked: Too many failed attempts: the terminal blocks access for 60 seconds.
barrierErrors.not_configured: The terminal is not configured yet: set it up on the Configuration tab first.

terminal.notFound: This terminal is not in the list.
terminal.offline: The terminal does not answer at {{ip}}. Check power and network; if its address changed, scan the network on the Terminals page.

configure.otpHelp: Briefly press the BOOT button on the terminal (less than 2 s). The display shows “Setup code: 123456” for 120 seconds. Enter that code here.
configure.urlHint: https:// address of your check_card endpoint (up to 350 characters).
configure.apiKeyHint: Sent as the x-api-key header (up to 64 characters).
configure.barrierHint: Sent as the Authorization header; also protects this terminal's API.

ca.bundle: Use the built-in public CA list

configure.caHint: {{n}} / {{max}} characters. Needed for private or self-signed certificates.
configure.wifiHint: Only for the Wi-Fi build of the firmware. Leave empty for Ethernet.
configure.saved: Saved. The terminal uses the new settings now.
configure.savedRestart: Saved. The terminal restarts to join the new Wi-Fi network.

errors.required: Server URL, api_key and barrier are required.
errors.urlLong: The URL is longer than 350 characters.
errors.urlScheme: The URL must start with https:// and contain a host.
errors.urlSpace: The URL must not contain spaces.
errors.secretLong: api_key and barrier may have at most 64 characters.
errors.control: Control characters (line breaks, tabs) are not allowed.
errors.caPem: The CA certificate must be in PEM format (-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----).
errors.caLong: The CA certificate is longer than 3800 characters.
errors.ssidLong: The Wi-Fi name may have at most 32 characters.
errors.passNoSsid: A Wi-Fi password needs a Wi-Fi name.
errors.passLength: The Wi-Fi password must have 8 to 63 characters.
errors.otp: Enter the 6-digit code shown on the display.

authModes.otp: First setup: code from the display

configure.savedBarrierHint: The barrier saved for this terminal is used. Leave “barrier” below empty to keep it.

diagnostics.needBarrier: Save this terminal's barrier to see its diagnostics:
diagnostics.stacksHint: Free stack per task. Below {{n}} bytes is a warning sign.

testServer.lead: A check_card server on this computer. Point a terminal at it, tap cards and watch every request.
testServer.provisionHint: Open a terminal, go to Configuration and press “Use the test server”: it fills in this URL, the keys below and the CA certificate.
testServer.checkAuth: Reject requests with a wrong api_key or barrier (401)
testServer.delayHint: The terminal gives up after 5000 ms.
testServer.asciiWarning: The terminal's font has only Latin letters: other characters are shown as “?”.
testServer.noRules: No rules yet: every card gets the “Unknown cards” answer.
testServer.recentUnknown: Recently seen cards without a rule:
testServer.logEmpty: No requests yet. Tap a card on a terminal that uses this server.

firmware.confirmOverwrite: Terminals that contain the old public key will reject images signed with the new key until they are flashed over USB again. Continue?
firmware.noKeys: No signing key yet. Create one; the private key stays on this computer (app/data).
firmware.step1: Replace the OTA_PUBLIC_KEY_PEM line in firmware/nfc_terminal/api_task.cpp with the code below.
firmware.step2: Build the firmware and flash it once over USB.
firmware.step3: From then on, upload new firmware here. Images with any other signature are rejected.
firmware.updateHint: Choose the compiled image (e.g. build/nfc_terminal.ino.bin). It is signed on this computer and sent to the selected terminal, which checks the signature and restarts.
firmware.uploaded: Installed ({{bytes}} bytes). The terminal is restarting.

errors.not_esp32_image: This file is not an ESP32 application image.
errors.no_barrier: Save this terminal's barrier first (Overview tab).
errors.barrier_rejected: The saved barrier was rejected. Enter the current one on the Overview tab.

signing.lead: The key that signs firmware for over-the-air updates. Install updates from a terminal's page, or for several terminals at once from the table.

serial.lead: Read the terminal's log over USB, straight from the browser.
serial.unsupported: This browser has no Web Serial support. Use Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer.
serial.hint: Close other serial monitors (Arduino IDE) first: only one program can use the port.

integration.lead: What your server has to implement so terminals can check cards against it.
integration.flow1: A card is tapped. The terminal reads its UID.
integration.flow2: The terminal sends one HTTPS request to the configured URL and waits up to 5 seconds.
integration.flow3: Your server decides and answers with an HTTP status and an optional message.
integration.flow4: The terminal shows green or red, the message, and is ready for the next card.
integration.requestHint: uid is the card UID in upper-case hex. Check both headers: they identify the terminal.
integration.rTimeout: “Connection Error”; the terminal re-checks the server every 15 s
integration.messageRules: Optional JSON body. Only Latin letters, digits and punctuation are shown, up to 76 characters.
integration.testYourServerHint: Send the same request the terminal sends:
integration.epConnect: Store server URL, keys, CA and Wi-Fi
